liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Viola Lee Blues** (3 reviews): A fourteen-minute version is described as loud, raucous, and similar to a jet taking off; The reviewer expresses enjoyment for any Viola Lee Blues performance from this specific time period [6][11][13]
- **Ice Cream Break** (1 review): The track sounds like material from Infrared Roses, suggesting it may not be contemporary [8]

## The recordings

- **gd1966-03-12.doherty.winters.17681.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 15 songs; 66 min; rated 1.71/5 by 7 [1]. Said about its sound: The sound quality is noted as not bad, though the volume is mostly low [11]
- **gd1966-03-12.sbd.bershaw.9516.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 68 min; rated 4/5 by 7 [2]
- **gd1966-03-12.sbd.bershaw.5412.shnf**: soundboard; 3 songs; 28 min; rated 3.33/5 by 12 [3]. Said about its sound: The recording is praised for having great sound quality for a 1966 performance [4]

## Around the show

- Pigpen is highlighted as an underrated and awesome blues singer during this early jam session [4]
- David Lemieux and the Tapers Compendium disagree on the specific date of this Acid Test recording [6]
- Pigpen is characterized as funky as a chicken on Sunday morning with some ripple [9]
- The reviewer loves the banter and confirms the event was an acid test [13]
- The reviewer suspects this recording might actually be from a March 19, 1966 Carthay Studios show [7]
- This Viola Lee Blues is a different version than the previous three-song Pico Acid Test release [2]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1966-03-12.doherty.winters.17681.shnf**: taped by Source disc provided by Terry Doherty; transferred by EAC(secure, offset corrected), track spliting with CDWave, sector boundaries verified with shntool, and shorten encoding(MKW) by D.Winters - 11/01.; source: ??? > CD > EAC > CDWave > SHN [1]
- **gd1966-03-12.sbd.bershaw.9516.shnf**: transferred by Alan Bershaw; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: The eighth song is identified as a cover of Freddy King's Heads Up; The ninth tune is a standard blues, distinct from The Same Thing, with an unknown title [2]
- **gd1966-03-12.sbd.bershaw.5412.shnf**: transferred by Alan Bershaw; source: Soundboard [3]. Also: David Lemieux provided a complete set list, which conflicts with the official chronological compilation; The recording originates from the chronological compilation of Acid Test recordings in Tapers Compendium Volume One [3][5]
